topic.subject: social
topic.title: Panchayati Raj and local government
topic.scope: Gram Sabha, Gram Panchayat, sarpanch, Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad, urban local bodies, ward councillors

misconceptions.statement: The Gram Sabha is a small group of elected leaders who make all the decisions.
misconceptions.why: Students often confuse the 'Sabha' (assembly) with the 'Panchayat' (executive committee) due to the similarity in names.
misconceptions.fix: The Gram Sabha consists of all adults in the village who have the right to vote, not just a few elected members.

probe.question: Who attends the meeting of the Gram Sabha?
probe.wrong_answer: Only the Sarpanch and the five Panchs.

misconceptions.statement: The Gram Sabha only meets when there is a big problem or a disaster.
misconceptions.why: Students associate 'meetings' with emergency situations rather than routine governance.
misconceptions.fix: The Gram Sabha meets regularly to discuss development plans, budgets, and audit the work of the Gram Panchayat.

probe.question: How often does the Gram Sabha meet?
probe.wrong_answer: Only when the village faces a flood or a serious crisis.

misconceptions.statement: The Sarpanch has the power to do whatever they want with the village money.
misconceptions.why: Students often view the Sarpanch as a 'king' or 'boss' figure rather than an accountable representative.
misconceptions.fix: The Sarpanch must get the approval of the Gram Sabha for the budget and development projects.

probe.question: Can the Sarpanch spend village funds without asking anyone?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because they are the head of the village.

misconceptions.statement: The Zila Parishad makes rules for the Gram Panchayat to follow like a principal in a school.
misconceptions.why: Students use their school hierarchy experience to understand government structures.
misconceptions.fix: The Zila Parishad coordinates development at the district level and distributes funds, but it does not act as a direct boss to the village panchayat.

probe.question: Does the Zila Parishad control the daily work of the Gram Panchayat?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, it is the highest authority and gives orders to the village panchayat.

misconceptions.statement: Urban local bodies like Municipal Corporations are just bigger versions of the Gram Panchayat.
misconceptions.why: Students overgeneralize the function of local government without considering the difference between rural and urban needs.
misconceptions.fix: While both manage local needs, urban bodies deal with city-specific issues like sewage, street lighting, and waste management in densely populated areas.

probe.question: Is the work of a Municipal Corporation the same as a Gram Panchayat?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, they both do the exact same things, just in different places.

requires_topics: Key Elements of a Democratic Government
